checks.why: a function assigned onto an instance's member from outside its class (`inst._i.run = _run`, `inst._i.parse = lambda ...`) runs when that member is called, so a walk from the caller reaches it and not only the class body's def (#1283)

the alias `inst._i.run = inst._i.parse` carries what `parse` was assigned, so a call through `run` also reaches the parse lambda — through a bounded TypeVar parameter as through a plain annotation (#1283)

the assigned function has callers: every call through the member, including the lambdas typed only by the callable annotation of the name they are assigned to (an alias, inline, dotted, a bounded TypeVar alias, a callback Protocol) (#1283)
